key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules from molecular structure, closely matching TD-DFT behavior at much lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening and optical simulation of photoactive molecules for organic photovoltaic device design, reducing dependence on expensive quantum-chemical calculations.
method: Equivariant GNN predicts complex-valued, frequency-dependent polarizability tensors from 3D molecular geometry and UV-vis spectra.
Model captures both dispersive and absorptive optical response features.
Validated in downstream device-level optical simulations for organic photovoltaics.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic datasets using metrics including earth mover’s distance, and its device-level charge carrier generation rates agreed with TD-DFT results with R² = 0.94.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability and quality of 3D structures and training data, so out-of-distribution molecules or device conditions could still require TD-DFT verification.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
